verses.text: Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch when the deer have their young?
Can you count the months until they give birth? Do you know when the time comes?
They crouch down, give birth to their young, and their labor pains end.
Their young grow strong in the open fields. They go off and do not come back.
Who set the wild donkey free? Who untied its ropes?
I gave it the wilderness as its home, and the salt flats as the place where it lives.
It laughs at the noise of the city. It does not hear a driver shouting.
It roams the hills for its pasture and looks for anything green to eat.
Will the wild ox agree to serve you? Will it stay by your feeding trough at night?
Can you tie it with a rope to plow your fields? Will it pull a plow through your valleys behind you?
Will you depend on it because it is so strong? Will you leave your heavy work to it?
Can you trust it to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
The ostrich flaps its wings proudly, but its feathers are not like the stork's that care for its young.
It lays its eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the sand.
It forgets that a foot might crush them, or that a wild animal might step on them.
It treats its young harshly, as if they were not its own. It does not worry that its work might be for nothing,
because God did not give it wisdom or a share of good sense.
Yet when it spreads its feathers to run, it laughs at the horse and its rider.
Do you give the horse its strength? Do you clothe its neck with a flowing mane?
Do you make it jump like a locust? Its proud snorting is terrifying.
It paws the ground in the valley and is glad about its strength. It charges out to meet the weapons.
It laughs at fear and is afraid of nothing. It does not run away from the sword.
The quiver of arrows rattles against its side, along with the flashing spear and javelin.
It races wildly over the ground. It cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.
When the trumpet blows, it snorts, 'Aha!' It smells the battle from far away. It hears the commanders' shouts and the battle cry.
Is it your wisdom that makes the hawk fly and spread its wings toward the south?
Does the eagle soar at your command and build its nest up high?
It lives on the cliff and stays there at night, on a rocky peak where it is safe.
From there it looks for food. Its eyes see it from far away.
Its young ones feast on blood. Where there are dead bodies, the eagle is there."
